title: Printing and Comments
description: println versus print, escape sequences for quotes and tabs, and notes that Java ignores.

items.title: println
items.text: Prints, then moves to a **new line**.

items.title: print
items.text: Prints and **stays** on the same line.

content.title: One letter of difference
content.caption: `print` is handy when you ask a question and the user types on the same line. You'll do that in Module 3.

steps.note: `print` writes `Hello, ` and stays on the line. The line isn't finished yet.
`println` adds `!` and then ends the line.

content.title: Building one line
content.outro: Four instructions, two lines of output.

content.question: What does this print?
options: `AB` on one line, then `C` on the next
content.explain: `print` stays on the line, so `B` follows `A`. `println` then ends that line, so `C` starts a new one.

content.value: Inside a print you can join pieces of text with `+`. Java sticks them together in order, with **no extra spaces**.

parts.label: a space
parts.note: The only space in the result comes from here.

content.title: Joining three pieces
content.caption: Want a space? Put it inside quotes.
A number joined to text becomes part of the text. Module 2 shows when that helps and when it catches people out.

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: `+` adds no space. To get `Hi there`, put a space inside one of the quotes.

content.value: A backslash `\` means "treat the next character specially". This is called an **escape sequence**.

items.sub: a double quote, without ending the text

parts.label: new line
parts.note: Two characters in the code, one line break in the output.

content.title: A new line inside the text

content.caption: `\n` works the same in `print` and `println`. Use whichever keeps your code easiest to read.

content.real: A sticky note on a recipe
content.text: The cook reads the recipe and ignores the note. Java does the same: a **comment** is a note for humans, and Java skips it completely.

content.caption: `//` starts a note that runs to the end of the line. `/*` and `*/` wrap a note over several lines.

content.value: Putting `//` in front of a real instruction switches it off without deleting it. This is called **commenting out**. Write comments that explain **why**: `// bonus point for a fast answer` beats `// add 1 to score`.
content.title: Two good habits

content.question: What does this print?
content.explain: The `A` line is commented out with `//` and the `C` line sits inside `/* */`. Only `B` runs.

practice.question: Use two `print` calls and one `println` so the output is exactly one line reading: Java is fun!
Print this exactly, quotes included: My teacher said "well done" today.
Print a two line shopping list using a single `println` with `\n` in the middle: Bread on the first line, Milk on the second. Add a comment above it saying what it is.

quiz.question: What does `System.out.print` do differently from `System.out.println`?
options: It does not move to a new line afterwards.
quiz.explain: `print` leaves the cursor on the same line, so the next output continues it. The `ln` in `println` is the new line.

quiz.question: What does this print?  `System.out.println("Game" + "Over");`
quiz.explain: `+` joins the pieces with nothing in between. A space has to be written inside the quotes: `"Game" + " " + "Over"`.

quiz.question: How do you print a double quote inside a piece of text?
options: Use two double quotes in a row.
You cannot print a double quote.
quiz.explain: The backslash tells Java the next character is part of the text rather than the end of it, so `\"` prints a quote.

quiz.question: What happens to a line starting with `//`?
options: Java prints it as a message.
quiz.explain: `//` starts a comment: a note for people reading the code. The compiler skips straight past it.

quiz.question: Which escape sequence starts a new line?
quiz.explain: `\n` is a new line, `\t` is a tab, and `\\` prints a single backslash.
